sentences.text:
1. The present appeal is filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 11.02.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi),
Kachchh in MACP No.29 of 2000.

2. Briefly stated, it is the case of the appellant that on 14.09.1999 at about 19 hours, while she, along with Ladharambhai, was going from Nani Khakhar to Talwana on scooter No. GJ 12 E 631, which Ratanben Devshi Patel vs Not Known on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17992150/
1 was driven by Ladharambhai and the claimant was a pillion NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1459/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined rider, at that time the truck No. GJ 12 V 6312 came from Mandvi side in rash, negligent manner and in excessive speed and lost control over the steering and collided with the scooter.

sentences.text: In the accident, the original claimant-apellant herein sustained serious injuries over the different parts of body.
Hence, the appellant filed the aforesaid claim petition for compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- from the respondents jointly and severally.

3. Vide the said impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the present appellants - original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding the present appellant- original claimant entitled to an amount of Rs.86,700/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petition till its actual realization with proportionate costs.
4. This Court vide order dated 23.06.2014 noticing the submissions made by the learned advocate for the appellants- original claimants and the grounds raised in the appeal, has admitted the appeal.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Samee Uraizee for Mr. Mehul Shah, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, while assailing the impugned judgment, has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1459/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined perspective.
It is contended that the Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the appellant as well as period of actual loss of income.

It was further contended that as the claimant was working as a agriculturist and earning Rs.70000/- to Rs.80,000/- per annum, the income of the claimant ought to have considered Rs.70,000/- per annum instead of just Rs.2000/-
per month by the tribunal by considering the evidence placed on record.
That, the tribunal has not considered the disability certificate issued by the Dr. H M Hadiya at exhibit 50, and has erred in assessing the disability of the claimant at 30% functional disability.

It is argued by the learned Counsel that the tribunal has overlooked the settled principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in relation to calculation of future loss, application of appropriate multiplier and grant of compensation under the various heads such as PSS, Special diet and attendant charges and medical expenses.

6. It is further submitted that the Tribunal has awarded a meager and unrealistic amount under various heads without considering the financial dependency of the family members and the socio-economic background of the appellant.
The learned counsel has urged that the compensation awarded is not just, fair, and reasonable, and is liable to be enhanced in accordance with the settled legal principles.
Learned counsel therefore prays for enhancement of the compensation NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1459/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined amount by reassessing the same in accordance with law.

7. Learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati, appearing for the respondent no.3- Insurance Company has placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and vehemently argued that the compensation must be awarded as just, proper and reasonable and not higher side and further submitted that learned Tribunal, after appreciating the materials available on record,

2 awarded the compensation under each head is just, proper and reasonable and not required to interfere and lastly prayed to dismiss the appeal.

sentences.text:
8. Heard learned advocates for the respective parties on the disputes between the parties in narrow compass and perused impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation.
9.
As regards the income of the appellant is concerned, The appellant has not produced any proof of income.
To substantiate her claim that she was agriculturist and was earning Rs.70,000/- per annum, she has produced bills of seeds and pasticides.

However, In absence of any strict proof regarding her income produced on record and considering the age of the claimant as 61 years, as rightly held by the tribunal as NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1459/2014 JUDGMENT DATED:
07/08/2025 undefined per the evidence on record, the income considered by the tribunal as Rs.2,000/- is just and proper and calls no interference.

10. The appellant has produced the disability certificate at exhibit 50 given by Dr. H M Hadiya,
wherein the disability was assessed as 52%.
The said doctor was examined vide Exh.33, in his cross-examination, he has admitted that he has given the said certificate without proper medical assessment.
He has also admitted in his cross-examination that due to the old age, such disability may be found.
Hence, the finding given by the tribunal with regard to the assessment of functional disability at 30% is just and proper.

11. Noticing the fact that the deceased was aged 61 years at the time of accident, in light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 and the scheduled prescribed, the Tribunal has rightly applied the multipler of 7 for the calculation of the future loss of income.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the tribunal has rightly calculated the future loss benefit as Rs.2000/-*12*7*30% = Rs.50,400/-.
12.

So far as the compensation under the other heads such as pain, shock and suffering and special diet, attendant charges and transportation are concerned, considering the facts of the case, nature of injuries, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1459/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 07/08/2025 undefined medical treatment and physical pain and the emotional trauma endured by the appellant, a substantial enhancement under the abovementioned heads are deserves to be enhanced.
Accordingly, Rs.20,000/- towards Pain, Shock and Sufferings and Rs.7,000/- towards Attendance Charges and Rs.7,000/- towards rich diet are required to be given.
The medical expenses of Rs.23,300/- and actual loss of Rs.4000/- awarded by the tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required under that head.

13. Therefore, original claimants - appellants herein are entitled to enhanced amount as computed hereunder:
